episode_title: Are Attractions Becoming Video Games? with Calum Smail

real_qa.q: What makes Voxel Studio's approach different in creating immersive experiences for attractions?
real_qa.r: Voxel Studio positions itself at the intersection of creative and technology, able to speak both languages—to agencies about art and design, and to technical teams. The company prioritizes guest experience first and foremost, though this doesn't always happen when working with agencies under tight deadlines of two weeks versus having 18 months to develop the experience properly.
real_qa.requete: Voxel Studio immersive experiences creative technology

real_qa.q: Why is spatial audio underutilized in attraction design compared to visual technology?
real_qa.r: Calum notes that spatial audio is overlooked despite huge opportunity. He cites Darkfield's shipping container experiences using spatial audio headphones where visitors can hear sounds around them in 360 degrees, creating genuine wow moments. He also references Old and Talents, a scare maze using spatial audio, and his own background in music technology and nightclub production showed him audio's power, yet it remains underrated versus flashy visual tech.

real_qa.q: What was the Dexter immersive experience created by Voxel Studio and what recognition did it win?
real_qa.r: Voxel Studio created a week-long Dexter TV show immersive experience in Shoreditch through Fever for Paramount, featuring seven actor-led rooms with technical production, lighting, escape room design and software programming. The project won Ad Week's Best International Experiential Activation, and it sold out instantly with super fans who demanded flawless execution on timing, policies and technical delivery.
real_qa.requete: Dexter immersive experience Shoreditch Ad Week award

real_qa.q: How should attraction operators prioritize technology versus creative content when designing experiences?
real_qa.r: Calum advises not thinking about tech first—the wrong approach. Instead, think about the guest and what they would want to see, then the tech will follow. A great creative idea might turn out to need less expensive or less grand technology than initially assumed. The focus should be spending time on the creative concept rather than leading with technology.
real_qa.requete: attraction experience design guest first technology

real_qa.q: What emerging technology trends does Voxel Studio see as genuinely pushing boundaries in attractions?
real_qa.r: Calum distinguishes between long-standing tech like touchscreens and projectors that no longer wow audiences unless done at massive scale like Sphere or Cosm, versus genuinely new tech pushing boundaries. He cites examples like the new Peter Pan ride at Disney Sea using innovative technology, and robotic installations. He's particularly interested in tech that creates a 'wow' moment when entering a space, not tech that feels bolted on or flashy for its own sake.
real_qa.requete: new technology attractions Peter Pan Disney Sea boundaries

guest.bio_context: Calum Smail founded Voxel Studio a week before COVID and had to pivot immediately. The company creates interactive experiences for brand activations, museums, visitor centers and immersive theater. Smail studied music technology and started in the nightclub industry before founding Voxel, and he positions himself at the intersection of creative and technology capabilities.

real_quote: The guest experience should always come first and foremost. Think about the guest and what they would want to see, then the tech will follow.
